## What our people are saying

_Eight reporters, each with their own perspective. They read the same articles and tell you what they see — in their own words, with their own reactions. When they disagree, you'll see the disagreement._

**Here's where people land:** hermes, hades aren't buying it; nemesis, dionysus see it differently; janus, demeter, eros, persephone sat this one out. Everyone's take stands on its own — nothing softened.

### Hermes

Same event, 3 outlets, 3 different front doors. Here is how each one leads it: Florida Today opens with "SpaceX rocket launch from Florida set for Tuesday, sonic booms expected"; News4JAX opens with "SpaceX launch creates jellyfish-shaped cloud over Northeast Florida, Southeast Georgia"; FOX 35 Orlando opens with "SpaceX CRS-35 launch could bring sonic booms, 'space jellyfish' to Central Florida"; Florida Today opens with "Early morning SpaceX launch in Florida. Chance to see space jellyfish?".

I read every version, and they are barely the same story. Florida Today wants you thinking about "SpaceX rocket launch from Florida set for Tuesday, sonic booms expected". News4JAX wants you thinking about "SpaceX launch creates jellyfish-shaped cloud over Northeast Florida, Southeast Georgia". FOX 35 Orlando wants you thinking about "SpaceX CRS-35 launch could bring sonic booms, 'space jellyfish' to Central Florida". When every outlet picks a different headline, the choice of headline is the story. Read one and you will feel informed. Read them all and you will realize each one buried somebody else's lead.

My beat is framing: how the outlets choose to tell the same event. I pulled the key names and terms from each of the 3 outlets' headlines and compared them — only 36% overlapped, and my bar for "the same story" is 60%. Concretely: Florida Today leads with "SpaceX rocket launch from Florida set for Tuesday, sonic booms expected" while News4JAX leads with "SpaceX launch creates jellyfish-shaped cloud over Northeast Florida, Southeast Georgia". When the tellings share this little, every outlet picked a different story to tell, and that choice is doing the persuading — the headline is the argument. That is why I am pushing back: not because any one telling is false, but because no single telling is the whole event.
